rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 163.8, up from 49.2): the wider sensor spacing (1.5 cm, 16 mm footprints) raised progress to 0.70 on the oval, with one finish in 20 trials, and slalom and s-bend progress rose too. But every run still ends off-track with about one line-loss event and max_error near 0.061 to 0.064 m, the 0.06 m limit. Steering oscillation is low on slalom and s-bend (0.12 and 0.28), so the failure is lateral drift, not jitter. Sensing coverage was the first suspect and has been partly addressed, but line loss persists, so correction strength is now the likely limit. Evaluator feedback recommended testing kp 2.0 to 2.5 with kd 0.3 when line loss stays near 1 per run, and that is what I do here. Change: controller.kp 2.0 to 2.5, all else unchanged (sensor geometry, sensor_weights, kd 0.3, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.2, line_loss last_direction). This isolates the correction-strength hypothesis. Expected result: max_error drops below about 0.05 m, line_loss_events falls toward 0 on the s-bend and slalom, and progress on those tracks rises above 0.34 and 0.09. Risk: the oval showed steering_oscillation of 0.32, so the higher kp could increase jitter; kd 0.3 is kept to damp it. Base speed stays at 1.2, so completion within 3 s is still unlikely on the slower tracks; speed will be raised only after line loss is controlled. Hypotheses: (H1) kp is the main limit on lateral error; (H2) kd 0.3 is enough to keep oscillation below about 0.35 at kp 2.5. Measurements requested: progress, line_loss_events, max_error, rms_error, steering_oscillation, plus completion and completion_time, per track.
